response:
Treating this as a real PR rather than the Next.js learn fixtures it actually is. No finding is `severity: high`, so nothing technically meets a block bar — but two detector classes encode rules that *will* drift if merged as-is, so I'd hold them for changes. Counts and the rationale, grouped by detector:

## Block merge

**`duplicated_role_status_plan_check` (×2, medium, agent_risk 0.49)** — `crime_00071`, `crime_00072`. Status policy for `"pending"`/`"paid"` is compared in 4 files using 2 different expression shapes. This is the textbook case the detector exists for: the rules *will* diverge silently. Block until extracted into a single helper. The agent_risk is below the duplicate-block tier numerically, but the *kind* of risk (policy drift, not code drift) is what justifies holding the merge.

**`magic_domain_literal_scatter` (×1, medium, agent_risk 0.52)** — `crime_00051`. Same root cause as above: `"status"` scattered across 5 form/action files. Couple this with the role-check finding — fix together by introducing a status enum/registry. Without it, an agent extending invoice statuses next week will touch 5 files and probably miss one.

## Warn (land, then file follow-ups)

**`commented_out_code` (×10)** — 4 medium (`crime_00047-00050`, agent_risk 0.53), 6 low (`crime_00082-00085`, `00088-00089`, agent_risk 0.42-0.44). The medium ones are 30–38 line disabled blocks in `latest-invoices.tsx`, `revenue-chart.tsx`, `pagination.tsx` — agents *will* re-enable these. Quick effort, delete with the PR or open a cleanup ticket.

**`duplicate_component_shape` (×1, medium, agent_risk 0.49)** — `crime_00070`. Four near-identical form subtrees across create/edit forms. Warn; pair with the policy-check fix since they live in the same files.

**`design_token_escape` (×8, low, agent_risk 0.41)** — `crime_00090-00097`. Inline `px` values in form/login/skeleton components. Low individually, but they cluster in the same files an agent will copy-paste from — classic seed for token drift. Warn, address in a UI cleanup pass.

## Ignore (noise on this PR)

**`exact_duplicate_block` (×46, medium, agent_risk 0.54-0.55)** — `crime_00001-00046`. Dominates the report numerically, but the duplication is between `basics/*-starter` ↔ `basics/*-final` and `dashboard/starter-example` ↔ `dashboard/final-example`. That's deliberate parallel scaffolding, not a duplication bug. The right fix is a `.crimes/triage.json` entry suppressing duplication across `*-starter`/`*-final` sibling trees, not extracting a shared helper that defeats the pedagogy. Until triaged, these dominate the medium count and would drown the real signal above.

**`oversized_raster` (×6) + `raster_should_be_vector` (×12)** — `crime_00052-00069`, low, agent_risk 0.50-0.52. Asset hygiene; not a merge concern. The icon-sized PNGs are customer avatars (`amy-burns.png`, etc.) — those are photo-style raster portraits, so the "switch to SVG" suggestion is a false positive for this domain. Worth a triage rule for `**/customers/*.png`.

**`sync_io_in_hotpath` (×6, low, agent_risk 0.44)** — `crime_00073-00078`. All in `basics/*/lib/posts.js` — these are `getStaticProps`-time loaders for the Next.js blog tutorial. Sync `fs.readdirSync` at build time is idiomatic for this pattern; the detector is right to fire on the shape but wrong about the impact here. Ignore.

**`direct_date` (×3, low, agent_risk 0.44)** — `crime_00079-00081`. `new Date()` in an action handler and two `formatDateToLocal` helpers. Low; the test_gap of 0.5 is the only thing keeping it interesting. Ignore unless a unit-test pass is on the roadmap.

**`deep_import` (×2, low, agent_risk 0.43)** — `crime_00086-00087`. `react-syntax-highlighter/dist/cjs/styles/prism` is the documented import path for that library's themes. Confirmed false positive; add to triage.

**`singular_plural_type_mismatch` (×2, low, agent_risk 0.40)** — `crime_00098-00099`. `revenue: Revenue[]` — `Revenue` is the row type, `revenue` is the table; the name reads fine in context. Add `revenue` to `allowedNames` and move on.

## Meta-observation for the runner

A finding count of 99 with 54 medium / 45 low and 0 high, where 46/54 mediums are the same tutorial-scaffolding duplicate, is the failure mode the PRD warns about: signal drowned by a single detector firing on intentional duplication. The two real merge-blockers (`status` literal + `pending`/`paid` checks) are buried at positions 51, 71, 72 in the list. For this fixture, baseline triage rules or a `crimes diff` against the previous tree would surface the real signal more cleanly than `scan` from empty.
